checks.what: Ilkhanate (ulus-of-hulegu) takes from the nominal Mongol Empire, 1261, the cells it still holds in Anatolia, the Jazira, Mesopotamia, Iraq, Syria and the Armenian Highlands. The page supports the Anatolia, Iraq and Jazira part: infobox 'Independent khanate (1260-1335)'; 'After the Battle of Kose Dag in 1243, the Mongols under Baiju occupied Anatolia'; 'The Mongols administered Iraq, the Caucasus, and western and southern Iran directly'. It moved 1,698 cells: Turkey 1,436, Syria 249, Iraq 13. The Syria leaf alone moved 164 cells of inner Syria (Homs-Palmyra, 36-40E, 34-36N). Those cells came to the Mongol Empire from the Ayyubids under the 1260 Mongol keyframe and go to the Mamluk keyframe in 1272. The page contradicts Ilkhanid rule there: Hulegu was only 'briefly conquering Ayyubid Syria and Aleppo in 1260', was defeated at Ain Jalut, and the Ilkhanids 'were never able to gain and keep significant ground against the Mamluks'. The Battle of Ain Jalut page: Damascus fell to the Mamluks five days after 3 September 1260, Aleppo within a month.
checks.fix: Removed the leaf {"country": "Syria"} from the union and updated the region text and note. Now 1,534 cells pass. The 85 Syrian cells inside the Jazira and Mesopotamia regions still pass. The 164 inner-Syria cells stay with the nominal Mongol Empire 1261-1271, as in the published draft (see problems). Anatolia goes to the Ilkhanate as direct land, although the page has Rum as a Mongol vassal; that is a Rum keyframe matter, and the label is better than 'Mongol Empire' either way.

checks.what: ulus-of-jochi takes from the Mongol Empire, 1271, its cells in the Volga region, Bashkiria and Volga Bulgaria: 601 cells, lon 43-59E, lat 54.6-58.5N. That covers north Bashkortostan (185 cells), Mari El, north Tatarstan and Udmurtia, and the Volga-Vetluga side of Nizhny Novgorod. The page supports it: 'After the division of the empire in 1259, it became a functionally independent khanate'; Batu was 'first conquering the Bashkirs' land and then moving on to Volga Bulgaria in 1236'. 1271 is a technical date: an earlier event would be undone, because the Jochid 1267 keyframe releases these cells and the Mongol 1270 keyframe picks them up. In the trial no later keyframe takes them back.
checks.fix: none. Residuals, not caused by this entry: about 311 cells (154 in 1265-1269) are still Mongol Empire land 1260-1270. About 155 Nizhegorod cells are Russian princely land drawn as Jochid direct land; the Vladimir-Suzdal dossier request should claim them.

checks.what: Mongol Empire vassal_end over Novgorod and Pskov (1285 shapes) in 1241. It cancels the tributary tint that mongol-empire/ledger/58 bridged on the Cliopatria gap. That bridge's own note admits it has no year: 'agreed to pay tribute' (no year on the page). The Alexander Nevsky page: 'In 1259, he led an army to the city of Novgorod and forced it to pay tribute it had previously refused to the Golden Horde'; the page has no capture of the city. The Golden Horde page: 'The Mongols abandoned their plan to capture Novgorod'; 'The Novgorod region in the far northwest was not counted until the winter of 1258-1259'. In the trial the 1241 net change is 399 cells: the Pskov and Votia occupation ends, which the Novgorod dossier's own ledger 6-7 also date to 1241. The other ~1,800 cells simply stay direct. No side effect.

ulus-of-jochi vassal_start over Novgorod and Pskov in 1259 (2,204 cells), closed by the ulus's end in 1293 as the old relation was. The pages support it: forced tribute 'to the Golden Horde' in 1259 (Alexander Nevsky), and the census reached Novgorod in the winter of 1258-1259 (Golden Horde). The suzerain is the Jochid ulus, not the Great Khan, which matches 'tribute ... to the Golden Horde'.

Second pass of events/0, dated 1271 because the 'Mongol 1270 keyframe re-adds ~1,500 cells in the Jazira, Mesopotamia and Syria'. The trial does not bear that out. The 529 cells it moved (Iraq 368, SE Turkey 129, Syria 32) are taken by the 1261 Mongol keyframe check: 399 of them from the Zengids of Mosul, 130 that nobody held. They then sit unchanged with the Mongol Empire 1261-1270; the 1270 keyframe adds nothing in this region. It also carried the same unsupported Syria leaf. Its page is the same as events/0 ('administered Iraq ... directly', independent from 1260).
checks.fix: Redated from 1271 to 1262 and removed the Syria leaf; the note and text were rewritten. Trial: the same 529 cells pass to Hulegu in 1262, and no Mongol keyframe (1270, 1279) takes them back. Iraq and Mosul are Ilkhanid from 1262, not 1271. The 32 Syrian cells (Hasakah/Deir ez-Zor) are still covered by the Jazira leaf.

checks.what: great-jin_1231 (1231-1232): the 1216 shape minus Hebei, Shanxi, Shandong, Shaanxi, Gansu, Ningxia and Inner Mongolia. It resolves to 853 cells: Henan 590 (contested) plus the Huai strip in north Anhui and Jiangsu, about 260. This carries out the dossier's own text 'Henan only'. The page: 'In 1231, the Mongols attacked again and finally took Fengxiang'; 'The Jin garrison in Chang'an panicked and abandoned the city, pulling back to Henan Province with all the city's population'. The page is silent on Gansu and Ningxia. Trial: 1231-1232 Jin falls from 1,369 to 853 cells, dropping Gansu 317, Ningxia 151 and Inner Mongolia 48, which become nobody's until the Mongol keyframe of 1234.

great-jin_1227 is a 'wrong' entry whose correction still applied over its data/shapes.csv years, 1227-1235, because do_keyframe unions every keyframe valid in a year. It is cut to 1227-1230, where the 1223 keyframe has the identical spec, so 1227-1230 does not change. In 1231-1233 the 1231 and 1233 keyframes now trim Jin. Trial 1233: Jin is the Caizhou district, 151 cells; before, it was 933 with Gansu, Ningxia and the Huai strip. The page has Kaifeng abandoned and the court at Caizhou, and the end on 9 February 1234.

house-of-ascania_1260 (1260-1271): the dossier's union with the unresolvable {place: Lauenburg} replaced by {region: Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg} (8 cells). The whole union resolves to 52 cells (about 13,150 km2): Anhalt towns, the 1363 Electorate of Saxony (Wittenberg) shape, Ratzeburg, Lauenburg, Weimar and Orlamunde. Trial: the house gets 16 cells in 1260, mostly the Wittenberg land from holy-roman-empire-minor-states. Anhalt and Holstein cells stay with their own dossiers. The House of Ascania page: John I and Albert II reign from 7 October 1260, 'Ruled jointly'; 'In 1296 Albert II and his nephews ... divided Saxony'; the Anhalt division of 1252; the map caption puts Lauenburg in the Ascanian duchy around 1235.

house-of-ascania_1272: same region and support as keyframe_overrides/2, 18 cells from 1272. The override gave no from/to, so it kept the shape's years in shapes.csv, 1272-1325. That reached across the window and, once resolvable, was unioned into the 1307 and 1315 keyframe checks of the next window. Its region still has Aschersleben (lost to Halberstadt 1315, ledger/3) and lacks Zerbst (gained 1307, ledger/2). The dossier's note for this shape says 'Valid 1272-1306'.
checks.fix: Added from 1272 and to 1306, and extended the why. This still reaches 1300-1306 of p1300-p1399, but that span has no Ascania keyframe check year, so there is no effect there. Trial unchanged in-window: 18 cells 1272-1299.

problems: Inner Syria (164 cells, Homs-Hama-Palmyra hinterland, 36-40E, 34-36N) is drawn as Mongol Empire land from the 1260 Mongol keyframe until the Mamluk keyframe of 1272. The Battle of Ain Jalut page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Ain_Jalut) has the Mamluks take Damascus five days after 3 September 1260 and Aleppo within a month, and a Mongol force beaten at Homs. Suggested entry: {slug: mamluk-sultanate, year: 1260, month: 10, type: gain, counterpart: mongol-empire, region: {minus: [{country: Syria}, {union: [{region: Jazira}, {region: Mesopotamia}]}]}}. The reviewer did not add it.

The 1261-1270 leftover of the Jochid ulus: about 311 Volga-Bashkir cells are Mongol Empire land 1260-1264 and 154 in 1265-1269. events/1 starts only in 1271 because the Jochid 1267 keyframe releases these cells.
